chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Meeting Billy Eckstine in Washington and Detroit
summary: Budd urges singer Billy Eckstine to come to Chicago and shares his Detroit hotel room.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And, I call him every time I go out there. And, so, I rejoined Earl. Well, we go back out on a tour. Now, by this time, Earl and Fox is falling out. Oh, incidentally, before this we were in Washington, D. C. And, I had met Billy Eckstine in Pittsburgh once when we played a dance there. But, then, see, Billy really lived in Washington with -- he lived there with his sister. She was a school teacher and he went to school in Washington. He stayed with

So, when we were getting -- we were -- just finished the Howard Theater and we're sitting out in the bus ready to leave back for Chicago, and -- and it was raining like mad. And, there was Billy standing up under the {inaudible} the shelter in the theater. And, I said, "Hey, there's Eckstein." I got out of the bus and went over there and was talking to him while we were waiting for the rest of the cats to get on.

I said, "Man, I heard you sing, man." I said, "You sure can sing. Why don't you come Chicago, man." He said, "Oh, man, me come to Chicago?" He said, "With all of those great singers you've got there?" He says, "Man, I wouldn't know what to do."

I said, "Man, you'll outsing all of these cats, if you come to Chicago." So, after that, I happened to be in Detroit and met Billy again. And, everybody got a room but me. But, he had a room in the Norris Hotel.
And, Actually, Billy was like emceeing and -- and dancing and singing down in the place called the Cotton Club there.
In Detroit. So, he says, "You don't have no place to stay, come up in my room. Stay with me." He says, "You can save that room rent anyway." I say, "Beau-
tiful." So, I stayed with Billy.

So, when we went up in his room, he said, "Man, I'm trying to look. I bought me a (Inaudible) little old trumpet here. I'm trying to learn how to play the trumpet." I said, "Yeah, I can help you a little bit on that." So, I started to show him something about the trumpet, and then showing him something about music, how to read music and spot time and what not.
So, he says, "You know, I think I'm going to take you up on that. I'm going to come into Chicago." So, after we went into Chicago, then sure enough Billy Ekstein came into Chicago.
